2027-07-26.title: Monday of the tenth week after Pentecost
readings: Godly grief produces a repentance that leads to salvation and brings no regret
“Jerusalem, Jerusalem”: Jesus longs to gather her children as a hen gathers her brood under her wings
2027-07-26.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Tenth Sunday after Pentecost. No commemoration is printed in the Panchangam today. In other calendars of the Church the parents of the Virgin Mary, Sts Joachim and Anne, are remembered on 26 July.
2027-07-26.verse: For godly grief produces a repentance that leads to salvation and brings no regret, but worldly grief produces death.
theo: Today's Epistle is a letter of relief after a hard season. Paul had written to the Corinthians a sharp letter that caused them pain, and for a while he wondered whether he had done right. Then Titus came back with good news, and Paul could say, “I rejoice, because I have complete confidence in you.” In the middle of that joy he explains why the pain was worth it: “For godly grief produces a repentance that leads to salvation and brings no regret, but worldly grief produces death.” There are two kinds of sorrow over sin. Worldly grief looks inward: it sulks, it makes excuses, it blames others, it sinks into shame and self-pity, and in the end it leaves a person more alone. Godly grief looks upward: it says, “I have sinned,” and gets up and goes to the one who forgives. Peter wept bitterly and came back to the Lord; the same night Judas was sorry too, but he looked at his sin and not at his Master, and despair finished what sin began. Paul lists what godly grief produced in Corinth: “what earnestness … what eagerness to clear yourselves … what longing, what zeal.” A good confession leaves us lighter, more alive and more eager to love.

In the Gospel some Pharisees come to Jesus with a warning: “Get away from here, for Herod wants to kill you.” They may be sincere friends. Jesus is not frightened. He calls Herod “that fox” and says that he will go on “casting out demons and performing cures today and tomorrow, and on the third day I finish my work.” He is not on Herod's timetable but on his Father's, and the road runs to Jerusalem, “because it is impossible for a prophet to be killed outside of Jerusalem.” Luke has already told us that “he set his face to go to Jerusalem” (Luke 9:51). Then the voice of the Lord changes from calm to tender: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to it! How often have I desired to gather your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!” This is the lament of a son of Israel who loves the holy city. The Church teaches that what was done in his Passion cannot be charged against all the Jews of that time or against the Jewish people today (Nostra Aetate 4); the Gospel shows how deeply the Lord loved the city to the end.

In Kerala we have all seen a hen when the monsoon rain comes down: she spreads her wings and the chicks run in, until only small beaks and feet show from beneath her. That is how God longs to gather us, and the sentence that grieves him is the last one: “you were not willing.” God is never unwilling; the only closed door is ours. Godly grief is simply the moment when we stop being unwilling and run under the wings. The passage ends with a promise: you will see him “when you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.’” At every Holy Qurbono we say it, and he comes.
outline: Ask: when I fall, do I run away from God or towards him?
Worldly grief turns inward and leads to death; godly grief turns to God and leads to salvation.
Point 2 · The fox and the road
Jesus follows his Father's timetable to Jerusalem, unafraid of Herod.
Point 3 · The hen and her brood
God longs to gather us; the only barrier is “you were not willing.”
live: Think of one failing you have been brooding over and take it to the Sacrament of Reconciliation this week, instead of carrying it alone.
When you feel afraid or ashamed today, stop and pray one sentence: Lord, gather me.
2027-07-26.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you longed to gather the children of Jerusalem as a hen gathers her brood, and you long to gather us. Turn our sorrow for sin into the sorrow that leads to life, and make us willing to come to you. Give us the courage to follow you on the road you walked, unafraid of the fox, and let us live under the shelter of your wings. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono the Church sings the welcome that Jerusalem sang: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; the one who longs to gather his children under his wings gives himself to us as the bread of life.

quick: Paul says that godly grief leads to repentance and salvation, but worldly grief leads to death.
Jesus is not afraid of Herod; he goes on his way to Jerusalem and teaches that the Father's work comes first.
Jesus longs to gather the children of Jerusalem as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, but they were not willing.
2027-07-26.action: Say a prayer of sorrow for one fault today, and then go and put it right.
2027-07-26.question: When I have failed, do I run away from God or towards him?

family.explain: Have you ever seen a mother hen when it rains? She spreads her wings wide and all her chicks run under them and stay warm and dry. Jesus says that is how much he wants to take care of us. When we do something wrong, he does not want us to hide from him. He wants us to run to him and say sorry, and he will gather us close.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who has hurt someone, that they may have the courage to say sorry.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anything I need to say sorry for tonight?”

illus: A boy in Thrissur hit a cricket ball through a neighbour's window. For three days he hid in the house, angry with himself, picking at his food. On the fourth evening his grandmother sat beside him and said, “Your sorrow has been eating you. Let it walk you to the neighbour's door instead.” He took his pocket money and went. The neighbour, who had already guessed, laughed, gave him tea and refused the money, though the boy insisted on coming the next Saturday to sweep the yard. Years later he said it was the lightest he had ever felt in his life. The first kind of sorrow had kept him in the house; the second took him out the door.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you long to gather us as a hen gathers her brood. Give us the sorrow that leads to life, and make us willing to come to you. Amen.
share: Godly grief produces a repentance that leads to salvation (2 Corinthians 7:10). When have I felt that kind of sorrow, and what came of it?
I rejoice, because I have complete confidence in you (2 Corinthians 7:16). How does it feel to be trusted, and whom can I trust more?
How often have I desired to gather your children together, and you were not willing (Luke 13:34). Where am I unwilling today?
pm.resp: Lord, gather us under your wings.
interc: For the Church, that she may always be a mother who gathers all her children.
For those who are ashamed of what they have done, that they may find the courage to return to the Lord.
For priests who hear confessions, that they may be gentle and faithful ministers of God's mercy.
For the city of Jerusalem and all who live there, Jews, Christians and Muslims, that it may know the things that make for peace.
For families who have lost a child or a parent, that they may find shelter under God's wings.
pm.close: Father, you long to gather all your children as a hen gathers her brood. Give us the sorrow that leads to life, make us willing to be gathered, and let us enter your house, blessing the one who comes in your name. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul tells the Corinthians that there are two kinds of sorrow. Worldly grief produces death; godly grief produces a repentance that leads to salvation and brings no regret (2 Corinthians 7:10). When I have done wrong, worldly grief makes me hide, blame and sink into shame. Godly grief makes me stand up and go to the Lord, who is waiting.

Think of Peter and Judas. Peter wept bitterly, and the Lord took him back; Judas looked at his sin and not at his Master, and despair finished the work of sin. The Sacrament of Reconciliation is the road of Peter: we confess, and we are lifted up and made lighter.

In the Gospel Jesus is warned that Herod wants to kill him, and he is not afraid. He goes on towards Jerusalem on his Father's timetable. And then he weeps over the city: How often have I desired to gather your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing (Luke 13:34). The Church teaches that the guilt of his Passion belongs to no people but to all of us as sinners.
So today let us stop being unwilling. Let us run under his wings, as chicks run to the hen in the monsoon rain. Let us go to him with our sorrow and receive his mercy. Amen.
kids: Children, have you ever seen a mother hen when the rain comes? She calls her chicks, and they run quickly under her wings, and soon you cannot see them at all! Jesus says that is how much he loves us. When we do something wrong, he wants us to run to him, not away from him. Say, “Sorry, Lord,” and he will keep you warm and safe. And remember to say sorry to the person you hurt too.

intro: Theme: “Godly grief produces a repentance that leads to salvation.”
On Monday of the tenth week after Pentecost: two kinds of sorrow, the Lord who does not fear the fox, and the hen who gathers her brood.

q: The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.
Just so, I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance.
points.apply: Take one burden you have carried alone to the Sacrament of Reconciliation this week.

points.h: The Lord who sets his face
q: I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame;
When the days drew near for him to be taken up, he set his face to go to Jerusalem.
points.apply: When fear tells you to turn back from something good, pray for the courage of the Lord who set his face.

sub: How often have I desired to gather your children.
Under his wings you will find refuge.
q: he will cover you with his pinions, and under his wings you will find refuge;
As he came near and saw the city, he wept over it,
points.apply: Each time you feel afraid or ashamed this week, say: Lord, gather me.

concl: Godly grief is simply the moment when we stop being unwilling and run to the Lord who longs to gather us.
He sets his face towards Jerusalem for us, and under his wings we find refuge.
2027-07-26.resolve: Choose godly sorrow, run to the Lord with it, and let him gather you.
